abstract: We prove algebraicity of rational Hodge morphisms between surface cohomology blocks that admit algebraic transfers through a fixed rank-one CM summand of a curve's first cohomology. For tensor spaces $L\otimes H^1(B)$, compatibility with the CM field forces every coefficient map to preserve weight-one Hodge types; divisor correspondences then realize the map. Hodge splittings extend this conclusion to surface blocks without presuming their algebraicity. The method proves that every Hodge map between odd transcendental parts of cyclic quartic covers $r^4=x^3+ax+b$ is algebraic, and gives the analogous conclusion for nontrivial order-three parts of cyclic sextic covers. Within either family, pairs whose elliptic quotients have geometric genus zero satisfy the rational Hodge conjecture. Applications include quartic-cover families of unbounded geometric genus and all smooth weighted sextics $r^6=x^3+a_4(w,t)x+b_6(w,t)$ with $(p_g,q,K^2)=(3,0,3)$. A finite-monodromy and invariant-cycle argument also treats CM-compatible maps on primitive-order-ten parts of $r^{10}=x^3+ax+b$, using incidence correspondences and an extension lemma for global forms. Separately, explicit products of curves dominate the elliptic K3 surfaces $y^2=t^n+x^3+ax+b$ for each fixed $7\leq n\leq12$ and $(a,b)\ne(0,0)$. Their graph retractions and one Fermat divisor bridge prove the Hodge conjecture for every pair in the union of these six families, allowing different exponents and imposing no polarization-similarity assumption. Known prime-order product-quotient K3 models give further compatible-pair applications. Exact formula and character checks accompany the proofs. Arbitrary higher mixed products, the exceptional degree-$44$ correspondence, and the general conjecture remain outside the conclusion.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
change_summary: Retains the quartic theorem and its split-embedding interpretation. Adds the sextic selected-part theorem and pair applications, including smooth weighted sextics with (pg,q,K^2)=(3,0,3), using global invariant cycles and a fixed-form extension lemma. Generalizes the centralizer to a fixed rank-one CM summand of curve H1 and proves compatible-map algebraicity for primitive-order-ten surface parts via divisor incidence correspondences. Proves pair-product HC across the full union y^2=t^n+x^3+ax+b, n=7,...,12: explicit product sources give the fixed-exponent case, invariant ranks exclude cross-maps except (8,12), and an explicit degree24 Fermat divisor bridge handles that case. Includes compatible prime-order product-quotient K3 applications, precise literature comparison and seven exact verifiers. Retains the unresolved degree44 and higher mixed-product boundaries.
title: Hodge correspondences through fixed CM curve factors
